description.short_caption: Bacterial growth on MacConkey agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a MacConkey agar plate with visible bacterial growth. The colonies appear as smooth, round, and pinkish in color, indicating lactose fermentation. The plate is uniformly streaked, suggesting a streak plate technique was used for isolation. The pink coloration of the colonies is characteristic of lactose-fermenting Gram-negative bacteria, such as Escherichia coli.

Case_15006/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of colony growth from blood culture.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli from colony growth.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of bacterial colony growth, likely from a blood culture. Numerous gram-positive bacilli are visible, appearing as pink to purple rod-shaped organisms scattered across the field. The background is clear, and the organisms are evenly distributed, suggesting a pure culture. The staining technique highlights the morphology and arrangement of the bacteria.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT of the chest showing a fluid collection with an arrow indicating the lesion.
description.detailed_description: This coronal CT image of the chest shows a hypodense fluid collection in the right thoracic cavity, adjacent to the pleura. The lesion is marked with an arrow, suggesting its clinical significance. The ribs and vertebral column are visible, providing anatomical context. No contrast enhancement is evident in this image.

description.short_caption: CT of the abdomen showing a hypodense lesion in the right psoas muscle.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a hypodense lesion in the right psoas muscle, indicated by an arrow. The lesion appears well-defined and is consistent with a possible abscess or fluid collection. Surrounding structures, including the spine and adjacent musculature, are visible. No contrast enhancement is evident, suggesting this is a non-contrast study.
